clue.text: Music from Dolly, maybe: number and track?

parts.note: a count is a number, as in a head count
RY is the crossword abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of song Dolly Parton might play: a numbered piece on an album track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' and 'track' look like music words in the surface, but they are a total (COUNT) and a railway (RY).
explanation.definitionFit: Dolly Parton is the best-known example of a country-and-western singer, so her music is an example of the genre.

clue.text: Plant went through expansion

indicators.note: one piece going through another sits within it, so the word for went is put inside the word for expansion

parts.note: a swell is an expansion or bulge
'went' in its slang sense of urinated gives PEED

explanation.surface: A plant that shot up and spread out, growing through a phase of expansion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went' looks like plain movement, but here it is the euphemism for relieving oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell is a small blue-flowered plant of the genus Veronica, a common wildflower.

clue.text: Cashiers come with me!

definitions.meaning: to cashier someone is to dismiss them, so he lets them go

explanation.surface: Bank tellers being told to follow someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cashiers' looks like bank tellers, but it is a verb: dismisses from service.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismissing an employee is letting them go, and the same phrase with an apostrophe is the everyday call to leave together.

clue.text: Cut up about housing mum, they mark locations in America

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so the quiet word goes within the reversed letters
about means turned round, so the pair of words is read backwards

parts.note: to snip is to cut
taken as written
mum means silent, and SH is the call for silence

explanation.surface: Someone cutting up and caring for their mother; the tail end turns to maps in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like mother, but it means quiet. 'about' turns the cut-up pair round to PUPINS before 'housing' takes in the hush.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a pushpin is a drawing pin with a raised head, used to mark places on a map.

clue.text: Film the usual Street of Nightmares interrupting rest

parts.note: par is the normal or usual level, as in 'below par'

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so the street goes inside the phrase for the rest

parts.note: the rest are all the others
the horror film A Nightmare on Elm Street names the street

explanation.surface: Bad dreams on a familiar street keep breaking up someone's sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rest' looks like sleep, but it means everyone else; 'interrupting' breaks into that phrase with the tree-named street from the horror film.
explanation.definitionFit: Parallel Mothers is a 2021 drama by the Spanish director Pedro Almodóvar.

clue.text: Lift given to Yankee spirit — or better

indicators.note: in a down clue a lift raises the letters, so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: a Yankee is an American, from the US
a peri is a fairy or spirit of Persian legend
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American is offered a drink of spirits, or something better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift given to' reverses US to SU in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Superior means of higher quality, so it is a synonym of better as an adjective.

clue.text: In which both paid and unpaid compete for a million

definitions.text: In which both paid and unpaid compete

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
taken as written

explanation.surface: A contest where professionals and amateurs play for a million-pound prize.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a prize of a million; the words are PRO, A and M.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro-am event, often in golf, puts professional players alongside amateurs in the same competition.

clue.text: It's impossible for me to learn over and over

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for learn is read backwards

parts.note: to con a lesson is to learn it by heart
taken as written
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone protesting that they cannot learn something however many times they go over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' appears twice: first it reverses CON to NOC, then it is O, the cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: No can do is a colloquial refusal, saying that a request cannot be carried out by the speaker.

clue.text: Broadcast Q&A relating to one telling tales of macabre bird

indicators.note: broadcast means put out over the air, so these words are heard rather than read

parts.words: Q&A relating to one telling tales of macabre
parts.note: the question 'Who?' answered by 'Poe', Edgar Allan Poe, writer of macabre tales

explanation.surface: A radio question-and-answer session about a writer of horror stories.
explanation.walkthrough: The question is 'Who?' and the answer is 'Poe', author of grisly tales like The Tell-Tale Heart; said together they make the bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The hoopoe is a crested Eurasian bird with pinkish plumage and barred black-and-white wings.

clue.text: Upbraid agent, film producer and studio executive

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is an agent
Hal Roach was the Hollywood producer and studio boss behind Laurel and Hardy

explanation.surface: Someone tells off an agent, a movie producer and a studio boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film producer and studio executive' is one person, Hal Roach, not two.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproach is to scold or criticise, a direct synonym of upbraid.

clue.text: Like a submarine? Tongue the filling for Sunday sandwiches

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between, so the language goes inside the filling
the filling of a word is its inside, everything but its first and last letters

parts.note: Erse is a tongue, the Gaelic language of Ireland or Scotland

explanation.surface: Tongue as the meat in Sunday's sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' looks like the cold meat, but it is a language. 'the filling for' keeps Sunday's inner letters, which 'sandwiches' wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine travels beneath the waves, so it is an undersea vessel; the question mark marks the definition by example.

clue.text: Gypsy very soon runs to the West

indicators.note: in an across entry going west means right to left, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: in a mo, short for in a moment, means very soon
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A traveller will shortly head westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the West' reverses IN A MO plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romani are a traditionally travelling people, often called Gypsies; the word also names one of them.

clue.text: Book women in Tier #50 the Leader of the Pack

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for women within the run of other pieces

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
the hash sign stands for number, abbreviated NO
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Reserve places for women in a seating tier numbered fifty, with the pack leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts W between NO and L. Brownies are the junior branch of the Girl Guides, organised in packs.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown Owl is the traditional title of the adult who leads a Brownie pack.

clue.text: Short cut suggested by Johnson, Cameron and chums?

definitions.text: Short cut suggested by Johnson, Cameron and chums?

parts.words: Short cut suggested by Johnson, Cameron and chums?
parts.note: Boris Johnson and David Cameron were both pupils at the famous public school, so a haircut fit for them would be named after it

explanation.surface: A quick route proposed by two former prime ministers and their friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short cut' looks like a quicker route, but it is a short haircut. Eton College is the elite school both prime ministers attended.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eton crop is a very short, slicked-down women's hairstyle fashionable in the 1920s.

clue.text: Was mum beaten in knockout?

indicators.note: in places the word for beaten inside the competition

parts.note: a cup is a knockout competition
to lam is to thrash, so beaten gives LAMMED

explanation.surface: Was mother defeated in a knockout tournament?
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like mother, but here it means silent.
explanation.definitionFit: To clam up is to refuse to speak, so someone who clammed up kept quiet.

clue.text: Sorting letters here won't stop

indicators.note: sorting means rearranging into a new order, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A mail centre where sorting goes on round the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorting' does double duty: it shuffles WONT STOP and paints the scene of a sorting office.
explanation.definitionFit: A post town is the town named in a British postal address, where mail for the area is handled.

clue.text: Here you may see each and every person sweep round?

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the word for sweep goes round the word for everyone

parts.note: a broom sweeps; to broom is to sweep
everyone is all

explanation.surface: A dance hall where everyone sweeps round the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweep round' looks like dancing, but 'sweep' is a cleaning tool and 'round' puts it about everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballroom is a large room for dancing, a place where couples glide round the floor.

clue.text: William Tell has no desire to break record

indicators.note: breaking the letters scatters them into a new order
has no means lacks, so the word for desire is taken out of the name

parts.note: will is desire, as in 'against her will'

explanation.surface: The Swiss archer is reluctant to break a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no' removes WILL from WILLIAM TELL, and 'to break' rearranges the remaining IAMTELL.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-time high is a record one, so the adjective means unsurpassed, record-breaking.

clue.text: Personal assistant yet to arrive, discovered someone else!

indicators.note: discovered means with the cover taken off, so the outer letters go

parts.note: someone yet to arrive is not here

explanation.surface: Someone finds their assistant has not turned up yet, and a stranger is there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' strips the outer letters P and E from PA NOT HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A. N. Other is the British placeholder name used on team sheets for an unnamed or yet-to-be-chosen person.

clue.text: Into swinging? This setter won't half rub it in!

indicators.note: swinging means moving loosely about, so these letters change order

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as ME

indicators.note: half here takes the back two of the four letters

explanation.surface: A setter boasting he will certainly gloat over his liking for swinging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swinging' rearranges INTO to OINT. 'won't half' is British slang for 'certainly will', but here it gives the second half, NT.
explanation.definitionFit: An ointment is a salve whose purpose is to be massaged into the skin.

clue.text: This I wantonly ruinate

indicators.note: wantonly means recklessly, so the letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A confession: this is what I recklessly destroy.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of RUINATE are the answer plus I, so the I in the clue is taken out of the anagram. 'This' points to the answer, which the whole clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue paints the natural world as the thing humans recklessly despoil, so the pointer word stands for the environment.

clue.text: Settle in

definitions.meaning: to land or settle, as a bird does
a fire that is in is still burning

explanation.surface: An instruction to make oneself at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle in' reads as one phrase, but it splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds come down and perch, and a fire still burning is said to be in, meaning lit.

clue.text: Stupid over-inflated self-importance when cycling?

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round from one end to the other

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize, too big
ego is an inflated sense of self

explanation.surface: A cyclist with an inflated ego looks stupid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when cycling' moves the leading OS of OSEGO to the end. 'Stupid' is a noun here, as in 'Come here, stupid'.
explanation.definitionFit: A goose is a silly person, so calling someone stupid as a noun is calling them a fool.

clue.text: Still with it, her toe-tapping covers

indicators.note: covers means holds within, so the answer lies inside these words

explanation.surface: A trendy woman still taps her feet to cover versions of songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' sounds like cover versions, but it signals that the letters run inside 'with it, her toe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitherto means up to now, the same sense as still in 'still waiting'.

clue.text: In on one bust, find me in a cell

indicators.note: In tells us the following pieces go inside the word for on

parts.note: re means on, concerning
I is the Roman numeral for one
a bust is a bosom

explanation.surface: Someone on a bust (an arrest) is told they will find the speaker in a jail cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' suggests a police raid, but it is a chest; 'In' at the start puts the numeral and that chest inside the word for on.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribosomes are the tiny structures in a living cell that build proteins.

clue.text: Sandwich service in which menu's been stripped of regulars

indicators.note: in which says the other letters go inside the service

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

indicators.note: removing the regular letters leaves the alternate ones, every second letter

explanation.surface: A sandwich bar where the menu has lost its usual items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped of regulars' looks like losing loyal customers, but it drops the odd letters of the fodder; 'in which' puts what is left inside the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Reuben is an American hot sandwich of corned beef, Swiss cheese and sauerkraut on rye.

clue.text: Redistributing made sense, American having left more than one estate

indicators.note: redistributing means sharing out anew, so the letters are put in a new order
having left means gone away, so that letter is taken out

explanation.surface: Land reform made sense once the American had gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having left' removes A from MADE SENSE, and 'Redistributing' rearranges MDESENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A demesne is land held by a lord, an estate; the plural matches 'more than one'.
